entities.summary:
The Institut de Droit International is a learned society of international lawyers founded in 1873 to promote the progress of international law. Long associated with Swiss and Belgian meeting places, including Grez-Doiceau connections, it gathered elite jurists to draft resolutions influencing treaties and doctrine.

In an era before dense international organisations, the Institut’s private scholarly diplomacy helped professionalise ius gentium and earned the 1904 Nobel Peace Prize. Its yearbooks and commissions shaped debates on war, neutrality, and arbitration.

The Institut shows how nineteenth-century bourgeois learned societies could act as soft legislators of international order.
